rationales: Cellulose is the main structural component of plant cell walls.
Peptidoglycan is found in bacterial cell walls.
Cholesterol is a membrane lipid, not a plant cell-wall component.
Chitin is found in fungal cell walls and arthropod exoskeletons.
Nucleoplasm is the fluid inside a cell nucleus.
Cytosol is the fluid portion of the cytoplasm, not the chloroplast.
Stroma is the fluid-filled interior of a chloroplast.
Cytoplasm is the material inside the cell membrane, outside the nucleus.
Metaphase I is when homologous chromosome pairs line up at the cell equator.
Chiasmata form during prophase I as homologous chromosomes cross over.
Telophase I occurs after homologous chromosomes have separated.
Anaphase I is when homologous chromosomes move to opposite poles.
Carbohydrates are not the main molecular category of enzymes.
Most enzymes are proteins.
Nucleic acids are not the main molecular category of enzymes.
Lipids do not generally function as enzymes.
Starch is a large carbohydrate polymer, not a three-carbon molecule.
Ribose contains five carbon atoms.
Glucose contains six carbon atoms.
Pyruvic acid contains three carbon atoms.
7.02 kcal is not the standard textbook value for energy released by ATP hydrolysis.
7.03 kcal is not the standard textbook value for energy released by ATP hydrolysis.
7.20 kcal is not the standard textbook value for energy released by ATP hydrolysis.
ATP hydrolysis is conventionally given as releasing about 7.3 kcal per mole.
12% is higher than the typical lipid content of milk.
10% is higher than the typical lipid content of milk.
0.9% is lower than the typical lipid content of whole milk.
Milk typically contains about 4% lipids.
Pericycle cells lie inside the root and do not form root hairs.
Stomata are pores typically found on aerial plant surfaces, not root hairs.
Root hairs are extensions of root epidermal cells.
Cortical cells lie beneath the epidermis and do not form root hairs.
Botany is the scientific study of plants.
Zoology is the study of animals.
Anatomy studies the structure of organisms or their parts.
Histology studies tissues.
Taxonomy classifies and names organisms.
Sedimentology studies sediments and sedimentary processes.
Genetics studies heredity and variation.
Paleontology is the study of fossils and ancient life.
A hypothesis is a tentative explanation of observations.
An experiment tests a hypothesis or investigates a question.
Deduction is reasoning from general principles to specific conclusions.
A theory is a well-supported explanation, not merely a tentative one.
The Indus dolphin is an endangered species in Pakistan.
Cows are domesticated livestock, not an endangered species in Pakistan.
Sparrows are not generally classified as endangered in Pakistan.
Markhor has conservation significance, but the expected endangered-species example here is the Indus dolphin.
Aristotle did not discover cells.
Robert Brown discovered the cell nucleus, not cells.
Robert Hooke described cells after observing cork.
Schwann contributed to cell theory but did not discover cells.
Christian de Duve, whose name is rendered here as Rene de Duve, shared the 1974 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.
Camillo Golgi received the Nobel Prize in 1906, not 1974.
Lamarck did not receive the 1974 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.
Aristotle lived long before the Nobel Prizes were established.
Mitosis produces two daughter cells, not one.
One cell divides into two daughter cells during mitosis.
Four daughter cells are typically produced by meiosis, not mitosis.
Mitosis does not produce eight daughter cells from one cell.
